messages.subject: process: patches to makefile
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

On Thu, May 23, 2013 at 10:53 PM, bgoodri <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
I agree that changes to the makefile generally aren't safe and should be
made to pass test-all. However, changes to make clean-all are safe enough
to just verify that make clean-all continues to work. If some make target
were depending on the clean-all target, we would have bigger problems that
are unrelated to the patch. Same with make help I guess.

=). The thing is... I can't guarantee that I didn't do something really stupid with the makefile. Honestly, I can't tell if parts of the makefile was written by a crazy makefile ninja or just a crazy person. This is why I am adamant about verifying that patches work by actually running the tests.


Do you know of any way of creating unit tests for makefiles?


 
On Thu, May 23, 2013 at 10:49 PM, Daniel Lee <notifi...@github.com>wrote:

> I think differently about these sorts of minor patches: they should all be
> tested.
>
> Any changes to the makefile are not safe. First, we don't have tests for
> the makefile itself and there's very little documentation. I've kept up
> with the user documentation as much as I could, but I haven't been good
> about the developer documentation. In this case, I can't see any issue with
> changing the clean-all target, but this could trigger some sort of
> dependency not existing which causes an error which may or may not happen
> on all platforms.
>
> With that said, I think it should work just fine. If it passes the tests,
> I'll merge it in. This change would have been exercised by clearing out the
> workspace's test directory while leaving it intact. The tests would have
> run after that change.
>
> —

Not necessarily. Bob and I stumbled on something yesterday -- if you look at src/stan/model/model_header.hpp.d, you can see that something's wrong there.

There are other weird little behaviors that indicate that something isn't quite right, like if certain files are laying around, make uses CC=c++ with no includes, not what's specified or the default in our makefile. I'm still not sure what's going on there.

And there's the issue with how long it sits and thinks before running test-unit again, which seems like there's something that may not be right.

With that said, maybe those aren't fundamental issues. It builds models fine. It runs tests. I'm just not sure if one of these issues are going to completely kill the build.
